Existing current facts about entities this note mentions:
- memory_id "1000917": The Boreal team observed on 2025-12-01 that the billing API's error rate crept up to 2 percent after the dependency bump.  (about: Boreal team, billing API, dependency bump)
- memory_id "1000867" [constraint]: The billing API has a deploy freeze from 2025-11-24 to 2025-12-02, during the peak season.  (about: billing API)
- memory_id "1000846": On 2025-11-04, the Ember team observed that the billing API's queue depth hit 50,000 following the marketing send, and since it was not their service, they flagged it.  (about: billing API, Ember team, marketing send)
- memory_id "1000841": The Boreal team observed on 2025-11-03 that the notification service's CPU sat at 90 percent after the traffic shift.  (about: Boreal team, notification service, traffic shift)
- memory_id "1000719" [decision]: The Cinder team owns the job scheduler as of 2025-09-23, when ownership transferred from the Dune team.  (about: Dune team, job scheduler, Cinder team)
- memory_id "1000715" [decision]: Ownership of the job scheduler transferred from the Dune team to the Cinder team on 2025-09-23.  (about: Dune team, job scheduler, Cinder team)
- memory_id "1000711": As of 2025-09-23, the pager for the job scheduler rings the Cinder team, not the Dune team.  (about: Dune team, job scheduler, Cinder team)
- memory_id "1000673": The Cinder team observed on 2025-09-03 that the authentication gateway's cold start time tripled after the runtime upgrade.  (about: authentication gateway, runtime upgrade, Cinder team)
- memory_id "1000662": The feature-flags service saw 40,000 requests per second at peak, most of them identical, as of 2025-09-02.  (about: feature-flags)
- memory_id "1000658" [decision]: Clients will cache feature-flags evaluations for 30 seconds, decided at the Atlas standup on 2025-09-02.  (about: feature-flags, clients)
- memory_id "1000645": The Dune team observed on 2025-08-19 that the resizer's cold start time tripled after the runtime upgrade.  (about: Dune team, resizer, runtime upgrade)
- memory_id "1000640" [constraint]: As of 2025-08-19, deploys to the job scheduler happen only on Tuesdays and Fridays between 09:00 and 10:30 UTC.  (about: job scheduler)
- memory_id "1000525" [decision]: The job scheduler is owned by the Dune team as of 2025-06-25, when ownership moved from the Ember team.  (about: Dune team, Ember team, job scheduler)
- memory_id "1000521": On 2025-06-25, Oskar walked Farah through the job scheduler runbook.  (about: Farah, Oskar, job scheduler)
- memory_id "1000474" [decision]: As of 2025-06-06, the job scheduler will use leader election instead of a single fixed node.  (about: job scheduler, leader election)
- memory_id "1000430": As of 2025-05-15, the pager for webhooks rings the Boreal team instead of the Ember team.  (about: Boreal team, webhook dispatcher, Ember team)
- memory_id "1000424": The webhook dispatcher is owned by the Boreal team as of 2025-05-15, when ownership moved from the Ember team.  (about: Boreal team, webhook dispatcher, Ember team)
- memory_id "1000384": The job scheduler depends on the feature-flags service.  (about: feature-flags, job scheduler)
- memory_id "1000378": The Cinder team reported on 2025-04-24 that feature-flags' p99 latency doubled after Tuesday's deploy.  (about: Cinder, feature-flags, Tuesday's deploy)
- memory_id "1000236": Boreal noticed the ledger service's memory growth and pinged the owners on 2025-02-21.  (about: Boreal team, ledger service)
Existing entity names: Boreal team, billing API, dependency bump, Ember team, marketing send, notification service, traffic shift, Dune team, job scheduler, Cinder team, authentication gateway, runtime upgrade, feature-flags, clients, resizer, Farah, Oskar, leader election, webhook dispatcher, Cinder, Tuesday's deploy, ledger service

"[2025-12-01] standup/boreal/2025-12-01-2: Boreal saw that the job scheduler's cold start time tripled following the runtime upgrade; not their service, so they flagged it."

New durable facts:
1. On 2025-12-01, the Boreal team observed that the job scheduler's cold start time tripled following the runtime upgrade. The fact is about Boreal team, job scheduler, runtime upgrade. They flagged it because it's not their service.

Entities: Boreal team, job scheduler, runtime upgrade. All exist in existing entity names.

Relations: Boreal team flagged the job scheduler? The note says "not their service, so they flagged it." This is similar to memory 1000846 about Ember team flagging billing API. That existing fact didn't include relations, just the fact. But we could add a relation "Boreal team flagged job scheduler" — the schema rel_kind examples: leads, maintains, owns, depends_on, member_of, reports_to. Flagging isn't really in those. In the existing memory list, similar observation notes (1000846) don't have relations. I think adding a relation here is optional; the guidance says "Add one for each relationship the note states." Does the note state a relationship? "not their service, so they flagged it" — implies Boreal flagged the job scheduler to its owners. Could add rel_kind "flagged" from Boreal team to job scheduler. That seems reasonable — rel_kind is "A short verb: leads, maintains, owns, depends_on, member_of." Flagged is a short verb. I'll add it.

Also possibly the job scheduler depends on... the runtime upgrade? That's an event, not a dependency. Skip.

Also could add relation: job scheduler affected by runtime upgrade? Probably overreach. Keep it minimal: one relation "flagged".

Actually, should I even add the relation? The example memory 1000846 says "since it was not their service, they flagged it" and no relations were recorded for it. But we don't know if relations were recorded. The instruction: "Add one for each relationship the note states." The note states Boreal flagged the job scheduler. I'll add add_relations with src "Boreal team", dst "job scheduler", rel_kind "flagged", evidence "not their service, so they flagged it".

Hmm, but maybe "flagged" isn't a durable relation. The pattern in existing memory seems to just record observations as facts. To be safe, I could include it; it's a relationship the note states. I'll include it.

Add fact:

entities: ["Boreal team", "job scheduler", "runtime upgrade"]
kind: "fact"
confidence: 1
evidence: "Boreal saw that the job scheduler's cold start time tripled following the runtime upgrade; not their service, so they flagged it."

The shortest quote supporting: "the job scheduler's cold start time tripled following the runtime upgrade; not their service, so they flagged it". Include date from note title [2025-12-01]? Evidence should be shortest span. "Boreal saw that the job scheduler's cold start time tripled following the runtime upgrade" — plus flagged part. I'll use the full relevant span.

No corrections needed — no contradiction with existing facts. There's a previous observation of resizer's cold start tripling after runtime upgrade (1000645), but that's different entity.

No aliases — "Boreal" refers to "Boreal team". The note says "Boreal saw". Existing entity name is "Boreal team". Should I add an alias "Boreal" -> "Boreal team"? The instruction: "When the note uses a different name for an existing entity, add an entity_aliases entry mapping the note's name to the existing name." The note uses "Boreal" while entity is "Boreal team". Past memory 1000846 text says "Ember team", 1000662 references... Existing entity names include "Cinder" and "Cinder team" separately. Hmm, "Boreal" vs "Boreal team" — I think adding alias "Boreal" -> "Boreal team" is appropriate. But in the fact content I should use the canonical name "Boreal team". Yes.
